test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Fitter) Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In triangle PQR, angle Q=90circ . If tan R=(1)/(2), then find the value of (sec P(3cos R-sin P))/(4csc R(4sin R-cos P)).
solution:
**Given:**

∠Q = 90°

tan R = 1/2

**Formula used:**

In a right Δ with ∠Q = 90°, P + R = 90° ⇒ P = 90° − R

So sin P = cos R, cos P = sin R, sec P = 1/cos P, csc R = 1/sin R

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let opposite to R = 1, adjacent = 2 ⇒ hypotenuse = √5

⇒ sin R = 1/√5, cos R = 2/√5, sec R = √5/2, csc R = √5

⇒ sin P = cos R = 2/√5, cos P = sin R = 1/√5, sec P = √5

⇒ 3 cos R − sin P = 3×(2/√5) − 2/√5 = 4/√5

⇒ Numerator = sec P × (3 cos R − sin P) = √5 × (4/√5) = 4

⇒ 4 sin R − cos P = 4×(1/√5) − 1/√5 = 3/√5

⇒ Denominator = 4 × csc R × (4 sin R − cos P) = 4 × √5 × (3/√5) = 12

⇒ Value = 4 ÷ 12 = 1/3

**∴ The value is 1/3.**
